To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the whole cell pertussis vaccine can act as an efficient adjuvant for a pneumococcal surface antigen and that a combined DTP-PspA vaccine can be used to prevent pneumococcal disease in children.
the combination of PspAs from the most prevalent serotypes with wPlow or wP as adjuvant, induced protection against pneumococcal infection.
the combination of PspAs with wP or wPlow confers protection against pneumococcal infection, with a role for antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a subunit pneumoccocal vaccine composed of PspA and wP or DTPlow that is safe, low cost and easy to manufacture.
the identification of new low cost adjuvant formulations to improve protection against pneumococcal infection, with potential applications in developing countries.
the development of a low cost and efficient vaccine against pneumococcal disease, which can be administered to children together with DTP vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of the currently available whole cell B. pertusssis vaccine with PspA could represent an effective and inexpensive strategy to prevent pneumococcal respiratory infections in children.
wPlow and wP are adjuvants to PspA5 that confer protection in mice against pneumococcal respiratory infections.
the combination of PspAs with wP or wP-low LPS confers protection against pneumococcal infection, and that the adjuvant effects are not mediated by LPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of PspAs with whole cell pertussis vaccine, either wP or wPlow, confers protection against a lethal pneumococcal respiratory challenge, and that this protection correlates with antibody responses.
the whole cell pertussis vaccine, either the classical one (containing high levels of B. Pertussis LPS) or the low LPS one, is an efficient adjuvant for PspA and that
the combination of PspAS and the whole cell pertussis vaccine increases protection against pneumococcal infection in mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of PspAs with whole cell pertussis vaccines can confer high levels of protection in mice against pneumococcal respiratory challenge, thus providing a low cost alternative for the development of new pneumococcal subunit vaccines.
wP and wPlow are good adjuvants that increase protection in mice against pneumococcal respiratory challenge.
wP can be used as an adjuvanted component for the development of subunit pneumococcus vaccine, and that this approach could be used to increase the protection of the current DTP infant vaccine.
